label: Power needed for flight grows as length^3.5 while muscle power grows as length^3
statement_en: A bird of fixed proportions must fly at a minimum speed proportional to the square root of its linear size, so the work needed for flight varies as the 3½ power of linear size while the work its muscles can supply varies only as the cube; flight thus becomes harder as birds get larger (about 1.4 times harder per doubling of length).

hypotheses.name: thompson1917-ch02-06#assumed-1
hypotheses.statement: Constant C_L,max across sizes (Reynolds effects change it), constant ρ, constant L/D, and flight at v_min rather than a faster, more efficient speed.

hypotheses.name: thompson1917-ch02-06#assumed-2
hypotheses.statement: The muscle premise of Thompson (muscle fraction f and mass-specific power p constant) is contested: contraction frequency falls with size, so the modern expectation is an exponent below 3. It is carried as a hypothesis, never proved or asserted.

hypotheses.name: thompson1917-ch02-06#assumed-3
hypotheses.statement: The physics thread found one Cypselurus hiraii specimen inside its v_min envelope (v_min 9.85 m/s against field speeds 10-20 m/s) but could not test the sqrt(W/S) scaling with its data; the theorems are statements about the model, not confirmed facts.

scope.basis: a theorem about a model: it applies wherever the design supplies the quantities it uses and accepts the hypotheses in scope.assumed
kernelChecked: Exact: lift = ½ ρ v² S C_L equal to weight with 0 < C_L ≤ C_L,max implies v ≥ sqrt(2W/(ρ S C_L,max)) (vmin_le).
Under R1, R2, constant ρ and C_L,max: v_min(L2)/v_min(L1) = sqrt(L2/L1), log exponent 1/2 (vmin_ratio, vmin_log).
With constant L/D, power required at v_min: ratio (L2/L1)^3 sqrt(L2/L1), log exponent 7/2 (powerRequired_ratio, powerRequired_log).
Under MusclePowerLaw (named hypothesis) and R1: power available ratio (L2/L1)^3 (powerAvailable_ratio); P_req/P_avail = c sqrt(L) with an explicit c (powerRatio_eq).
assumed: Constant C_L,max across sizes (Reynolds effects change it), constant ρ, constant L/D, and flight at v_min rather than a faster, more efficient speed.

The muscle premise of Thompson (muscle fraction f and mass-specific power p constant) is contested: contraction frequency falls with size, so the modern expectation is an exponent below 3. It is carried as a hypothesis, never proved or asserted.

The physics thread found one Cypselurus hiraii specimen inside its v_min envelope (v_min 9.85 m/s against field speeds 10-20 m/s) but could not test the sqrt(W/S) scaling with its data; the theorems are statements about the model, not confirmed facts.
